### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `create-objectstack`, `objectstack-blank`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/create-objectstack/README.md`, `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/AGENTS.md`, `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/README.md`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/getting-started/build-with-claude-code.mdx`  _(via exportsOf (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/your-first-project.mdx`  _(via exportsOf (symbol, a top-level const))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/create-objectstack/README.md`, `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/AGENTS.md`, `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/README.md`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5a6267f4862556fd7422cd161cd931b03aa17b72` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `eff30fa2412644f9cd7e917ccd8f34c2d92223b0` — the merge of head `702a27775dfda9c4bd3dc96f2fb775ba026c8de1` into base `5a6267f4862556fd7422cd161cd931b03aa17b72`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin eff30fa2412644f9cd7e917ccd8f34c2d92223b0 && git checkout eff30fa2412644f9cd7e917ccd8f34c2d92223b0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5a6267f4862556fd7422cd161cd931b03aa17b72 702a27775dfda9c4bd3dc96f2fb775ba026c8de1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5a6267f4862556fd7422cd161cd931b03aa17b72 && git merge --no-ff 702a27775dfda9c4bd3dc96f2fb775ba026c8de1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5a6267f4862556fd7422cd161cd931b03aa17b72
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5a6267f4862556fd7422cd161cd931b03aa17b72` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d50d46fe0da3a3192183393f6a4c824d93c9a940`

### ① Derived judgments

- **The static copy is bound to the single source. Correct.**
  - `packages/cli/test/create-objectstack-wiring-parity.test.ts` reads `SCAFFOLD_WIRED_BARRELS`, `SCAFFOLD_WIRED_REQUIRES` and `TEMPLATES.app.configContent`/`srcFiles` from `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts:602-703`.
  - It compares the sorted `BARREL_IMPORT`, `HELPER` and `STACK_KEY` lines with `toEqual`, checks `requires` as a superset, compares each empty barrel byte-for-byte, and adds vacuity guards.
  - Each kind of drift reddens it:
    - a generator added to `GENERATORS` (`generate.ts:559-577`) grows the roster, which reddens `toEqual` and the `%s exists` case;
    - a new token in `FLOW_SCAFFOLD_REQUIRES` reddens the superset check;
    - a reworded `renderEmptyWiredBarrel` reddens the byte compare;
    - a changed import style in `renderWiredImports` reddens the vacuity guard.
  - So it is not a silent second rule. The only designed slack: if a token is removed from the roster, the starter keeps its extra token (the superset check). That is acceptable, since the connectors need `automation`.
- **The six barrels are byte-identical. Correct.** Each file equals `renderEmptyWiredBarrel(stackKey, type)`'s output, article slip included ("a action", "a app").
- **The starter's other files are consistent.**
  - `blank/package.json` needs no new dependency, because the new imports are relative barrels.
  - `tsconfig.json` includes `src/**/*` and uses `moduleResolution: bundler`.
  - `objectstack.manifest.json` carries no `requires`.
  - `_gitignore`, `Dockerfile` and `ci.yml` are unaffected.
  - `blank-template-console-disclosure.test.ts` only asserts there is no `.app.ts`, so the empty barrels pass.
- **The providers resolve outside the monorepo. Correct by reading.**
  - `Serve.CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` (`serve.ts:1863-1937`) maps `automation`/`triggers` to `@objectstack/service-automation`, `trigger-record-change`, `trigger-schedule` and `trigger-api`.
  - They are loaded via `await import(pkg)` inside the CLI module, so they resolve from `@objectstack/cli`'s own `dependencies`, where all four are present in `packages/cli/package.json`.
  - A real starter installs `@objectstack/cli` as a devDependency, and its Dockerfile runtime image ships the CLI: the same path `automation` already used.
  - Not re-booted here. The dev's boot ran inside the monorepo, but the mechanism is location-independent.
- **The `'./src/objects'` import is safe.**
  - `moduleResolution: bundler` resolves the directory index.
  - Every starter script goes through `objectstack *` (an esbuild-loaded config) or `tsc --noEmit`. No script runs Node ESM on the config, and the starter ships no bundler.
  - The form is the one `os init` renders, and the parity pin requires it.
- **The `packages/cli` devDependencies are justified, and nothing published changes.**
  - `files` is `['dist','README.md','CHANGELOG.md']`, and `dependencies` is unchanged.
  - **Why the devDeps are needed:** the chain pin scaffolds under `packages/cli/node_modules/.create-objectstack-reach-*`, so Node resolves `@objectstack/connector-*` from `packages/cli/node_modules`. The devDeps put those packages in `@objectstack/cli#test`'s `^build` closure; temp-dir symlinks would not.
  - There is no cycle: no connector depends on `@objectstack/cli`.
  - **The lockfile** changes only the `packages/cli` importer block:
    - the keys are in pnpm sort order;
    - the `link:../connectors/connector-*` paths exist;
    - the header is unchanged.

    That is consistent with regeneration by tooling.
- **The `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` + `turbo.json` edits are minimal and correct.** They add two globs on the existing `@objectstack/cli` entry, plus a `heldBy` witness in the shape the file documents (`:87-95`, ten prior uses). `turbo.json` mirrors exactly those two globs. Nothing else under `scripts/` changed.
- **The `cli.mdx` walkthrough is true.**
  - `os generate object customer` yields `my_app_customer`.
  - `flow customer` writes `customer_flow`, bound to `my_app_customer` (`generate.ts:319-406`).
  - `action customer` writes `type: 'flow'`, `objectName: 'my_app_customer'` and `target: 'customer_flow'` (`generate.ts:277-317`), so "runs the flow" and the object-first ordering hold.
  - The fixture callout's "a second action and a `Logic:` row" is consistent.
  - The `os info`/`os compile` fixture blocks print `Runtime: 3 plugins` and no capability line, so `triggers` leaves them true.
- **`your-first-project.mdx` §2 is true.** The tree and the config code lines match the head template.
- **Overlap with open PRs: clear.**
  - #20341's `cli.mdx` hunks are at 1651, 1677 and 1685; this PR's are at 33, 739, 1410 and 1421.
  - #20258's `your-first-project.mdx` hunk is at lines 1-7; this PR's are at 91-160.
  - #20258 (265 files, three pages read) does not touch `cli.mdx`.
- **Docs made false: one was missed. Wrong.**
  - `content/docs/getting-started/build-with-claude-code.mdx:226-228` says that, in the `npm create objectstack` project of its step 1, the agent wires a new action, view and app "via the `actions:` / `views:` / `apps:` arrays in `defineStack()`".
  - On the wired starter, those keys are already `exportsOf(...)`. Following the line means writing a duplicate property or replacing the barrel wiring. The shipped `AGENTS.md` rule 3, rewritten in this PR, now says the opposite.
  - The PR body names this duplicate-key hazard as "inference, not measured" and leaves the page.
  - The `cli.mdx` fixture callout links to that section. #20258's hunk on the page is lines 1-7, so a fix is disjoint.

### ② Semver level

`create-objectstack: patch` is right: it is a bug fix to generated starter content.
- `create-objectstack` is in the changeset `fixed` group with `@objectstack/cli` (`.changeset/config.json:77`), so the group bumps together.
- `@objectstack/cli` gains tests and devDependencies only, with no published API change.

`Clause-②: no` is right: no accept set changes. Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Files outside the amended claim:** none, strictly. Claim `5861507334` (amended at 03:04Z, after the 03:02Z report) names every file in the 20-file diff. One soft stretch: the parity unit pin lives in `packages/cli/test/`, while the claim words the tests as "`packages/create-objectstack` tests, and one per-PR pin". It is declared in the PR body.
- **PR body vs diff:**
  - These match: the 20 parity cases (2+4+7+1+6), the 4 chain cases, the lockfile +9, the devDeps +3, and the scripts and turbo edits.
  - "Docs this change made false are corrected in place" is incomplete (see the bullet above).
  - The `'./src/objects'` import change appears in the report's deviation (2), but not in the body's "What changed".
- **`SKILL.md:192`:** confirmed stale on head (`requires: ['automation']`). It is governed and declared out. `skills/objectstack-platform/references/bootstrap.md:161-180` is a generic bootstrap, not the starter.
- **Not re-measured:** install, typecheck and boot of a fresh starter. The review relied on reading, plus CI's Scaffold with repo dist and the Test Core shards.
- **CI on head** (read last): 36 check runs.
  - 27 success and 0 failure.
  - 3 skipped: Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in) and Registry canary.
  - 6 in progress: Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core (1/6), Test Core (3/6), Test Core (5/6), Test Core (6/6), and Type Check · workspace.

  Both new pins run in Test Core shards that are still in progress.
